criteria.description: Correctly applies ML-01's reverse-mode rule to the MLP chain structure.
Correctly connects this to the delta-recursion and explains why the same machinery generalizes.

solutions.fullSolution: ML-01's reverse-mode rule applied to the MLP's chain graph (x0->z1->x1->...->f), working backward, gives exactly the delta-recursion delta_l=(W_l^T delta_{l+1}) elementwise-times sigma'(z_l). Backprop is reverse-mode autodiff specialized to this particular chain-shaped graph, which is why the same generic machinery (PyTorch) handles arbitrary architectures, not a separate neural-net-specific algorithm.

criteria.description: Correctly explains ordinary ridge needs phi(x)'s coordinates explicitly.
Correctly explains the dual form only needs inner products, computable via the kernel function directly.

solutions.fullSolution: Ordinary ridge's closed form needs phi(x)'s actual coordinates to build X and multiply by beta; infinite k makes this impossible directly. The dual form only needs inner products k(xi,xj), never phi(x)'s coordinates -- as long as k is cheap to evaluate directly, dimensionality of the implicit feature space doesn't matter.

criteria.description: Correctly verifies it numerically and explains the differing inverse sizes.

solutions.fullSolution: (X^T X + lam I)^-1 X^T = X^T(XX^T + lam I)^-1. Verified numerically for random 5x3 X, lambda=2: max abs diff ~1e-16 (machine precision); predictions computed both ways agree. Left side inverts a 3x3 matrix, right side a 5x5 matrix.

criteria.description: Correctly verifies the identity numerically for the new matrix.
Correctly identifies the 2x2 vs 4x4 inverse sizes and why the dual form is preferred when d>>n.

solutions.fullSolution: Verified to machine precision for random 4x2 X, lambda=1. Left side inverts a 2x2 matrix (d=2 features), right side a 4x4 matrix (n=4 samples). The dual form is preferred when d is much larger than n (or infinite), since the tractable n x n inverse is the one actually computed.
